title: Normalized ordinary finite tensor comparison is an isomorphism
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with geometric algebraic closure k, a prime l, and a finite extension E of Q_l with independent site and coefficient universes [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. For an arbitrary scheme automorphism g:Spec(k)->Spec(k) and a natural index n, let B_n be the constant sheaf of R/(varpi^(n+1)), let F_n be sectionwise inverse image with action transported through the inverse canonical coefficient map [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], and let P_n be the actual module pullback [def-pur-integral-finite-pullback]. There is a unique natural isomorphism e:F_n~=P_n such that, for every B_n-module sheaf M, every pro-etale U, and x in M(gU), e_M(U)(x) is the pullback adjunction-unit generator at gU restricted along the canonical comma arrow. This includes zero modules and arbitrary g, with no characteristic hypothesis.

proof.text: The recorded tensor-unit natural map has the displayed value on every section by its actual construction. Apply it termwise to a single-term complex in integer degree zero. The defining uniqueness of the complex comparison identifies the two maps. Invertibility of the recorded complex comparison yields invertibility of the ordinary component at zero, for every module. Componentwise invertibility makes the ordinary natural map invertible.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_tensor_comparison_iso_existsUnique (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! e : inverseImageFiniteModules.{t, u} l E g n ≅
        integralOperationsLevelPullback.{t, u} l E g n,
      ∀ (M : integralOperationsFiniteModules l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n)
        (U : (Spec (.of D.k)).ProEt)
        (x : M.val.obj (op ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U))),
        (e.hom.app M).val.app (op U) x =
          (((integralOperationsLevelPullback.{t, u} l E g n).obj M).val.map
            (proEtaleIsoCommaArrow g U).op)
            (integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E g n M
              ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U) x)

tool_uses.why: Uses only invertibility of the already specified finite tensor-unit comparison, for a single-term complex, to identify the two ordinary level functors; this is a generic pullback tool and does not replace any step of the trace-transport unit.
